sections_inspected: pp. 46–47, including the discussion of Judt’s use of Weber’s ethic of responsibility and the cited passage from Politics as a Vocation
scope_outcomes.criterion: A finding requires an explicit proposition-level stance by Riley toward a cited Weberian position, supported by a verbatim passage carrying the relevant actor, predicate, object and qualification.
scope_outcomes.basis: Riley explicitly says that Weber’s actual view was different from Judt’s gloss, reconstructs Weber’s account of political responsibility, and endorses Weber’s rejection of moralizing.
limitations: This outcome concerns the supplied citing text and the citation-stance dimension only; it does not represent Riley’s complete work or Weber’s entire reception.
Other Weber references in the article were not treated as positive findings where the supplied passage did not establish a proposition-level stance.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
